name: Campfire Trout with Wild Herbs
description: Freshly caught trout cooked simply over the fire with foraged herbs and butter.
method: Season the trout generously inside and out with salt and pepper.
Heat your pan until very hot then add a knob of butter.
Lay the trout in the pan and cook 4 minutes each side.
Add garlic and herbs in the last minute, basting the fish with the butter.
Finish with a squeeze of lemon and serve immediately.
tips: Make sure your pan is properly hot before the fish goes in — this is the secret to crispy skin that doesn't stick.

name: One-Pot Sausage & Bean Stew
description: A deeply satisfying one-pot stew that warms you from the inside out after a long day on the trail.
method: Fry the sausages in the pot until browned all over, then set aside.
Fry the diced onion in the same pot for 5 minutes until soft.
Add garlic and paprika, stir for 1 minute.
Add tomatoes and beans, stir well.
Slice the sausages and return to the pot.
Simmer for 15 minutes until thick. Season well.
tips: Tinned beans and tomatoes are camping gold — lightweight, no prep, and they make any stew instant.

name: Wild Bilberry Porridge
description: Creamy morning porridge topped with freshly foraged bilberries — a proper fell-walker's breakfast.
method: Bring water to a gentle simmer in your pot.
Stir in the oats and salt.
Cook for 5-7 minutes stirring occasionally until thick and creamy.
Serve topped with fresh bilberries and a drizzle of honey.
tips: Bilberries grow on the fell tops above 300m from late July to September. They're smaller and more intense than blueberries.

name: Lake District Lamb & Root Stew
description: A hearty stew using local Herdwick lamb and seasonal root vegetables — perfect after a long day on the fells.
localIngredients: Herdwick lamb from a local farm shop
method: Brown the lamb in batches in a hot pot — don't crowd the pan.
Add onion and cook until softened.
Stir in flour and cook for 1 minute.
Add stock, carrots, potatoes and rosemary.
Simmer with lid on for 35-40 minutes until lamb is tender.
Season well and serve with bread.
tips: Herdwick lamb has an intensely rich flavour from grazing the fells. Ask at any local farm shop — far superior to supermarket lamb.

name: Campfire Flatbreads
description: Simple two-ingredient flatbreads cooked directly on the griddle — endlessly versatile as a side or wrap.
method: Mix flour, salt and yoghurt into a soft dough — add a splash of water if too dry.
Divide into 4 balls and flatten each to about 5mm thick.
Cook on a dry hot griddle for 2-3 minutes each side until puffed and charred.
Serve warm.
tips: Works with plain flour too — just add 1 tsp baking powder. Wrap around anything for an instant camp meal.

name: Foil-Baked Salmon with Lemon
description: Salmon steamed in its own foil parcel over embers — incredibly moist with almost zero washing up.
localIngredients: Fresh salmon if near a river or coastal fishmonger
method: Lay each salmon fillet on a large piece of foil.
Top with a knob of butter, lemon slices, herbs, salt and pepper.
Wrap tightly into a sealed parcel.
Place on embers or grill for 12-15 minutes.
Open carefully — the steam is very hot.
tips: The foil parcel method works with almost any fish or vegetable. Check it's cooked by pressing — it should flake easily.

name: Camp Pasta with Pesto & Sun-Dried Tomatoes
description: The classic easy camp meal — pasta from a jar of pesto is unbeatable for speed, taste, and minimal kit.
method: Boil a pot of salted water.
Cook pasta according to packet instructions.
Drain, reserving a cup of pasta water.
Stir through pesto and sun-dried tomatoes.
Add a splash of pasta water to loosen if needed.
Top with parmesan.
tips: Pasta water is the secret — the starchy water emulsifies the pesto into a proper sauce rather than a dry coating.

name: Camp Shakshuka
description: Eggs poached in a spiced tomato sauce — one pan, minimal ingredients, and it works for breakfast or dinner.
localIngredients: Fresh eggs from a local farm shop
method: Fry diced onion in oil for 5 minutes until soft.
Add garlic, cumin and paprika, stir for 1 minute.
Pour in tomatoes and simmer for 8 minutes until thickened.
Make 4 wells in the sauce and crack an egg into each.
Cover and cook for 5-6 minutes until whites are set but yolks still runny.
Season and serve with flatbreads.
tips: Cover the pan with a lid or foil to trap heat and cook the egg whites without flipping.

name: Camp Fried Rice
description: Quick fried rice using whatever you have — the ultimate use-everything camp meal.
localIngredients: Fresh eggs from a farm shop
method: Heat oil in wok or pan until very hot — almost smoking.
Add rice and press flat, let it crisp for 2 minutes without stirring.
Push rice to the side, scramble eggs in the space.
Mix eggs through the rice.
Add peas, garlic and soy sauce, stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Finish with sesame oil and spring onions.
tips: Pre-cooked rice pouches are camping gold — no boiling needed and they fry perfectly. The high heat is essential for proper fried rice.

name: Foraged Mushroom Omelette
description: A golden omelette stuffed with freshly foraged mushrooms — the perfect woodland breakfast.
localIngredients: Wild mushrooms (porcini, chanterelles, or field mushrooms)
method: Fry sliced mushrooms in butter for 3-4 minutes until golden. Season well. Set aside.
Wipe pan, add more butter over medium-high heat.
Beat eggs with salt and pour in.
As edges set, push them to the centre with a spatula.
When almost set, add mushrooms and fold omelette in half.
Slide onto plate immediately.
tips: Only forage mushrooms you can identify with 100% certainty. Chanterelles, porcini, and giant puffballs are good beginner choices.

name: Steamed Coastal Mussels
description: Wild mussels steamed with white wine and garlic right on the beach — as fresh as it gets.
localIngredients: Fresh mussels gathered from rocks at low tide
shopIngredients: Glass of white wine or cider
method: Scrub mussels and remove beards. Discard any that won't close.
Fry garlic in butter for 1 minute.
Add wine and bring to a boil.
Add mussels, cover tightly and steam for 4-5 minutes.
Discard any that haven't opened.
Scatter with parsley and serve with bread to mop up the broth.
tips: Only gather mussels from clean water away from storm drains. Check local water quality notices. The rule: if it doesn't open, don't eat it.

name: One-Pot Vegetable Curry
description: A warming, fragrant curry using tinned chickpeas and whatever vegetables you have.
method: Fry onion for 5 minutes until soft.
Add garlic and curry paste, fry for 2 minutes.
Add tomatoes and coconut milk, stir well.
Add drained chickpeas and simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in spinach until wilted.
Serve with rice or flatbreads.
tips: Curry paste keeps for ages and is one of the best camping flavour shortcuts. Rogan josh, tikka masala, or Thai green all work.

name: Campsite Breakfast Hash
description: Crispy potatoes with bacon and eggs — the classic campsite fry-up in one pan.
localIngredients: Fresh eggs from a farm shop
method: Dice potatoes small and parboil for 5 minutes to speed up frying.
Fry bacon until crispy, set aside.
Fry onion and potato in the bacon fat until golden and crispy — about 10 minutes.
Make two wells, crack in eggs, cover and cook until whites are set.
Crumble bacon back over the top.
tips: Pre-boiling the potatoes is the key to getting them crispy in a reasonable time on a camp stove.

name: Ginger & Soy Noodle Soup
description: A restorative, warming noodle soup that comes together in minutes — perfect for cold evenings.
method: Bring stock to a boil.
Add grated ginger, garlic and soy sauce.
Add noodles and cook for 3-4 minutes.
Taste and adjust seasoning.
Serve topped with spring onions and a drizzle of sesame oil.
tips: Dried noodles and stock cubes are the ultimate lightweight camping ingredients — barely any weight and packed with flavour.

name: BBQ Corn with Herb Butter
description: Corn on the cob charred over the BBQ with a herb butter that melts into every crevice.
localIngredients: Fresh corn from a farm shop in late summer
method: Mix softened butter with chopped herbs and salt.
Grill corn directly on the BBQ for 10-12 minutes, turning regularly.
Rub generously with herb butter while still hot.
tips: Leave the husk on while grilling for the first 5 minutes to steam the corn, then pull it back to char the kernels.

name: Red Lentil & Vegetable Soup
description: A filling, nutritious soup that cooks quickly and uses entirely non-perishable ingredients.
method: Fry onion until soft, add garlic and spices.
Add lentils, tomatoes and stock.
Bring to boil then simmer for 20 minutes until lentils are soft.
Season well.
Blend partially if you want a thicker consistency.
tips: Red lentils don't need soaking and cook in 20 minutes — making them perfect camp food. They're also extremely lightweight to carry.

name: Camp Cheese Quesadillas
description: Crispy, melty quesadillas — the fastest hot camp meal you can make.
method: Mix drained beans with paprika.
Lay a tortilla in a dry hot pan.
Scatter cheese and beans over half.
Fold over and press down.
Cook 2 minutes each side until crispy and cheese melted.
Serve with sour cream.
tips: Hard cheese like cheddar travels well without refrigeration for a day or two. Grate it before you leave home.

name: Wild Garlic Pasta
description: Spring's great foraging gift — wild garlic made into a simple, pungent pasta sauce.
method: Cook pasta in boiling salted water.
Roughly chop wild garlic leaves.
Drain pasta, reserving a cup of water.
Toss pasta with wild garlic, olive oil and a splash of pasta water.
Cook for 1 minute until garlic wilts.
Serve with parmesan and lemon.
tips: Wild garlic carpets woodland floors from March to May. Look for the distinctive smell and broad green leaves with white star flowers.

name: Campfire Beef Chilli
description: A proper slow-cooked chilli with deep, smoky flavour — best made the night before and reheated.
localIngredients: Beef mince from a local butcher
method: Brown mince in batches until properly coloured.
Fry onion and garlic until soft.
Add spices and cook for 1 minute.
Add mince, tomatoes and beans.
Simmer on low heat for 35 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Serve with rice, flatbreads or jacket potato.
tips: Chilli genuinely tastes better the next day — make it on night one, reheat on night two for your best camp meal.

name: Camp Toasted Cheese Sandwich
description: The simplest camp comfort food — golden, buttery, crispy on the outside and molten cheese within.
method: Butter the outside of both bread slices.
Fill with sliced cheese and any extras.
Place butter-side down in a cold pan, then turn heat to medium.
Cook 3 minutes until golden, then flip.
Press down with a spatula and cook another 2 minutes.
tips: Starting in a cold pan means the bread toasts slowly and evenly without burning before the cheese melts.
